What happens when a sports game meets a house renovator? A game where you renovate old sports facilities! 

Restore the glory of sports in a [b]relaxing renovator sim[/b], made by Goat Gamez, a studio founded by Movie Games and [b]Robert Lewandowski[/b]!

Wishlist the game now:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2230960/Sports_Renovations/

How do you save your beloved team’s court from being torn down by a real estate developer? You do what you do best – renovate dilapidated sports facilities to collect the money you need to help out.

Restore gyms, courts, pools and pitches to their former glory, upgrade your tools and expand your headquarters. Collect trophies and mementoes during your renovation missions and display them proudly in a special room for everyone to see.

[b]FEATURES:[/b]

[list][*]Two game modes: Campaign with a predefined number of levels and storyline.
[*]Buy new tools and upgrade the equipment you already own.
[*]Earn money on your renovation jobs and use it to expand your own base of operations – each room unlocked will add some perks and some of the rooms come with a side mission.
[*]Buy cosmetic items you can place around your office.
[*]Trophy room where the player sees various memorabilia collected during renovation missions.[/list]

Are you ready to give sports facilities a second chance?

notes.title: The Fire Station – What can you do in your base of operations?
notes.notes:
Hi there!

Among all the preparations to release Fire Commander, we thought it’s a great idea to let you know more about your base of operations – the Fire Station. After all, we want you to be well prepared for your roles as commanders of your own firefighting units! So, what can you do there?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/bf8af314326a383c85fa3424b0b0a1671177abe5.png[/img]

The Fire Station is a very important part of every firefighter’s life. It’s a place to train, socialise and rest between missions. It’s the same in the game! 

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/mqUXMrNFh38pWvdBcB/giphy.gif[/img]

First and foremost, it is a place where you can hire new firefighters and choose the ones whose expertise you’ll need during a particular mission. Before starting a mission, check out the stats and skills of your available firefighters. Remember, deploy the ones best suited for the mission.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/7135dc8c30d1f01aec377f0ce3c9dbc3c4af3e37.png[/img]

When the mission is done, it is time to take care of your firefighters. There are a few rooms available for your people to use, like the gym or the social room. They serve to recover their health and stamina, improve their skills, and so on.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/tHk8XHN6dmQWuAddtD/giphy.gif[/img]

Remember to improve your Fire Station too! Each mission completed will earn you some money. Use it to hire new firefighters, upgrade the rooms to accommodate more units, and unlock new upgrades and skills. The more advanced your Fire Station, the better your chances to get a five-star completion status on your mission!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/bd7c338f7a6add179f8e6dc266c7d34e112cc337.png[/img]

Hope you find it helpful! See you soon.

notes.title: Not just Emergency – what inspired us?
notes.notes:
Emergency is most likely the first title gamers think of when it comes to firefighting – and for a very good reason. It is a real-time strategy game, where the player commands many different units from 4 branches (fire department, medical services, police and technical units) trying to resolve accidents of different kinds. Emergency was certainly a big inspiration for our game but also not the only one. Here are some more:

[b]Burn[/b]

A 2012 documentary film about Detroit’s firefighters. The city has been in severe decline in recent decades and by many, it’s been written off as dead. Many of the abandoned decaying buildings catch fire, turning into a more and more concerning problem. This film tells a story through the eyes of the personnel of the Detroit Fire Department, about their lives and their taxing battle on the front lines. They face constant emergencies, their budgets are shrinking, and the task is truly thankless. And yet, they preserve, determined to save the city at all costs.

[b]Benjamin Franklin[/b]

Yes, that Benjamin Franklin. Surprised? Did you know that in 1736 he co-founded the Union Fire Company, the first formally organized all-volunteer fire company in the colonies? That he did. It was the first fire company dedicated to protecting the entire community and later served as an example for other such companies. In 1730 a fire started on a ship and consumed all warehouses in the harbour and three neighbouring houses. Seeing the damage caused by fire, Franklin started advocating for community service to help extinguish fires to protect citizens’ properties. In 1733 he wrote an article in the Pennsylvania Gazette about how the colonies needed an organised group of citizens dedicated to fighting with fire. And so the first Fire Company was founded.

[b]The games of our youth[/b]

And there were many. The old close combat games, the first RTSs. The games we know and love. Who didn’t play StarCraft, slacked-jawed and awed about it then? Then more strategy RTS games came, management came in. More studios decided to make games about the police, firefighters, and so on. And they’ve stuck with us, so for certain, some of them became our inspiration, consciously or not.

These are some of our inspirations for Fire Commander. There are more, of course, as there is a lot of fantastic books, games and films about firefighters. What comes to your mind when you think about these heroes?

notes.title: Fire Commander – FAQ
notes.notes:
Hello, heroes!

Recently, we’ve gotten some good questions from one of our fans, [b]NitrouZ[/b], and we decided to fire some answers back. Here we go!

[b]Q: How big will the campaign be? How many missions can players expect?[/b]
A: At this moment we have more than 30 missions in a variety of environments. Some of the missions have major set pieces and story bits, some are smaller but still tense and challenging. Like a real firefighter, you don't just fight the biggest fires ever, but also respond to minor calls.

[b]Q: What kind of missions will there be? Only fires, missions without fire or also traffic accidents?[/b]
A: Not just fires or arsons. Traffic accidents, toxic spills, even a plane crash! I think you'll be satisfied with the variety.

[b]Q: What units and vehicles will there be? Do they have any special functions (dangerous goods, divers, etc.)?[/b]
A: There are different types of firefighters and vehicles, and moreover, they're upgradeable! We have medics, units specialized in breaking through obstacles, high-altitude people, water refill vehicles, ambulances, ladder trucks, water cannon trucks... But what we like about this selection is that every firefighter can do the other's work, at least to some degree, just not as skillfully. It's not like you have this one person that only takes care of the victims and is useless in other situations.

[b]Q: Will the units only be American or are there plans to offer units from other countries later on?[/b]
A: We based the game and the style on the American firefighting units, but it's a cool idea to introduce other nations, and we don't say 'never' to cool ideas. 🙂

[b]Q: Will modding be possible?[/b]
A: To make a game mod-friendly it's best to start making it with this intention because it changes the entire development philosophy. Fire Commander wasn’t made with modding in mind but we will see what the future brings.

[b]Q: Will there be film sequences for the various missions (e.g. events that could occur during a mission)?[/b]
A: Yes, we have introductions, voice-overs, cool cinematic shots et cetera, which goal is to add immersion and bring focus to what’s at stake. Mostly in the story missions, of course, which are perhaps a bit more 'out there' than your side missions in terms of spectacle. Bigger flames, Hollywood-style firefighting action! 🙂

[b]Q: What are the plans after the release? Are there plans for DLCs that will continuously expand the game?[/b]
A: The cool thing about Fire Commander is that it gives us so much freedom to take it beyond its initial setting. Buuuut, let's not commit to anything yet. We want the base game to be a full, complete product that you can fully enjoy without opening your wallet every 15 minutes.

[b]Q: What is the story behind Fire Commander?[/b]
A: If you mean the story of how the game came to be, it's just we thought that firefighters are kinda underappreciated. When you think about it, they are everyday heroes. Soldiers fight in wars and that's brave and all, but firefighters jump into fire pretty much EVERY DAY. They deserve their own game. And we liked the firefighting RTS games of the olden days, so we thought we could modernize the formula a bit.

[b]Q: Is the lighting of the vehicles still being worked on?[/b]
A: Everything is, really. 🙂 It's the question of managing your time and resources, which of course aren't endless. At this moment we can start polishing the visuals etc., but our priority were the mechanics. Until the game goes gold, we'll keep improving stuff.

[b]Q: Did the development take inspiration from other games?[/b]
A: Sure! I mean, we can't pretend Emergency doesn't exist. This was one of the games of our teenage years. We loved it, but even if we hadn't, we'd play it just to see what it did, and that'd also mean taking inspiration from it.

[b]Q: Will the turntable ladder be used to rescue people later on? Or will it only be used for extinguishing?[/b]
A: You can order your firefighter to climb it, take a victim, and bring it back down.
[b]
Q: There are already different extinguishing agents. What about ventilation in case of fires (e.g.: smashing windows and doors to avoid burn-through)? Will this feature be implemented?[/b]
A: I can't say for sure right now because it's not always obvious what works best. You'd think that a firefighting game should have these things, but once you start making it more realistic, it just becomes cumbersome and slow to play. That's why we don't have hoses. We tried them, but then it turned to Hose Deployment: The Game. It was slow, you focused on them too much, and it wasn't the game we wanted to make. So: we're trying stuff, we'll keep balancing it, but ultimately we want the game to be fun. We'll see! Work in progress.

We hope that answers some of your doubts or wonderings. If you want to help us, wishlist the game!
See you next time.

notes.title: Biggest Fires in History
notes.notes:
[b]Fire Commander is our way to celebrate the heroes of the real world. [/b]

For some time now on our Facebook and Twitter we’ve been remembering the greatest fires in history. Take a look at some of the events we’ve covered. 

If you’d like to learn more about real firefighting, consider following us, and add our game to your Wishlist.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/494edce6b425ba852588716b2754b2cc3c0fd907.jpg[/img]

This was a sad time for New York. The city still healing from a cholera epidemic suffered a [b]winter fire that covered 17 blocks.[/b] It all started in a warehouse, with strong winds spreading the blaze.

With the rivers frozen, fighting the fire was extremely difficult. Firefighters had to drill holes in the ice. [b]Water froze in transport.[/b] Buildings were blown up to create a debris barrier to stop the flames.

647 buildings destroyed. $20 million lost. Fortunately, only 2 people were killed. It was [b]the greatest fire to date[/b] in America's history.

In the aftermath, the city built aqueducts for quick water access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/b429e362760ebac48740ac14d89db0dbbc88851e.jpg[/img]

It was a terrifying and costly event in the history of Chicago. The Chicago Fire of 1871 [b]burned for two days straight[/b] in October.

It is said that the fire was caused by a cow kicking over a lantern in a barn. There are also other theories, one says it might have even been a meteor. The true cause of the fire has never been determined.

The fire [b]destroyed thousands of buildings[/b] in the Windy City and caused the death of around [b]300 people[/b] before the much-needed rain helped put it out. It also cost the city an estimated 200 million dollars in damages.

However great the losses, Chicago raised from the ashes like a phoenix. The reconstruction efforts began quickly and spurred great economic development and population growth.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/52b46069ccac887a298f607ea54ca0e3b8d3d4d9.jpg[/img]

Still fresh in our memory, the California wildfires of 2021 serve as a prime example of fire still being an untamable force of nature. Between January and October, there were more than 8,000 fires that burned over three times the area than in 2020.

The fire that destroyed over 1300 buildings--the largest one this year--is known as the Dixie Fire, named after the creek where it originated. It raged for months, from July 13th, and was finally put out only a couple of days ago, on October 25th.

The total area of the fire is larger than the entire state of Rhode Island. The fire significantly affected the quality of air in the entire Western United States.

The Dixie Fire will be known as the most expensive fire operation in California’s history to date.

notes.title: How fire acts
notes.notes:
Firefighters! 

Fire is a peculiar enemy to fight in a game. Is it even an enemy? It doesn’t have an artificial intelligence or a goal. It just… is. And it spreads in any manner it can., destroying everything in its way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/d2b66f3f7a956c87829cfc1ad85089f8a2f2396d.gif[/img]

We treat it as an enemy as it’s your direct target and opposition, and we’ve made sure that despite being an unmotivated force, it can surprise you and react to what you do. In the game, every surface is different, and it reacts differently to fire. It can combust easily or not at all. It can burn quickly or for a prolonged period. It can emit smoke or toxic fumes, et cetera.

There are different ways to extinguish the fire, depending on its type. You won’t put out an electric fire using water, for example. And if you start fighting it in one place, it can take a different route in some other part of the map. This makes fire a respectable enemy, and one that can make different playthroughs quite unique. Ultimately, how fire acts depends largely on you!

notes.title: Meet your heroes: Medic
notes.notes:
The Medic is one of the most important members of your crew. Medics can take care of incapacitated victims and assist them to the ambulance at a faster pace. 

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/pESJ1K8FgNTJ27bnXi/giphy.gif?cid=790b7611664ca847319d0c22a2c3575be0c07206faadde2c&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

notes.title: Between Duty and Life a.k.a. the Gameplay of Fire Commander | DevLog #1
notes.notes:
Hi, I’m Marek, the designer of Fire Commander. I’d like to tell you about our game: what it is, how it works, and how it came to be.

Let me start by saying that I find our game very special, and for many reasons. It’s the game I’ve been “destined” to make. At one point in my life I joined the Volunteer Fire Department, but I fell in love with it much, much earlier. One of my most vivid childhood memories is my first visit to the school library. The first book I’ve ever picked was--no surprise here--about a boy who becomes a firefighter. 

Fire Commander is the game I’ve wanted to play. It’s a tribute to my childhood (and adulthood) heroes. So what is it about, exactly? 

[h3]If you asked me to encapsulate Fire Commander within one genre, I’d call it a real time tactical game. [/h3]

I guess that would be fair, but then, it’s like calling Aliens just a sci-fi film. Well, yes, it is a sci-fi film, but this kind of pigeonholing gives you a very vague understanding of what makes it special. The soul is in the details, and in the case of Fire Commander, in the different levels of ‘scope’. 

There are three such levels in our game. The one you’ll see the most often in gameplay videos is the fire fighting missions. It’s where the tension is: [b]you control several specialized fire fighters, in some missions also vehicles, and have to tame the blazing inferno[/b]. Our game plays in real time and doesn’t have turns, but you still have to think about your every move and care for your teammates. More about it later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/0c856e653748c225ed620237fb9cceebf6ffd5cf.jpg[/img]

During missions, you can also use the active pause to collect your thoughts if the situation is getting out of hand. However, mind that [b]the pause doesn’t stop the game entirely[/b]. It slows it down to super slo-mo, but things are still happening, so you can’t just take a walk and think it over. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/5a5fe96aa0c0e67e4b2a29f2c4adb61109fc7b99.jpg[/img]

After all, you’re dealing with fire. Fire won’t give you a break. 

This is one of the elements of realism we’ve introduced. However, it’s a video game, so while we have been heavily inspired by the true heroes of our world, it’s not a perfectly faithful simulation of their work.[b] What we hope to simulate are the emotions of this profession[/b], the sense of responsibility, the respect that you need to have to the most dangerous element.

The second gameplay layer, placed above the missions but not as pronounced, is the overarching theme of [b]running your fire station[/b]. You get rewarded for completing missions, and the funds that you get help you equip the building and your crew. The deeper you go in the game, the more it becomes yours. We, the designers, simply present you with situations you have to face. It’s up to you to choose the approach. This also connects with the third layer. 

[h3]The third big aspect of the gameplay is maintaining the well-being and development of your crew. [/h3]

Each member can specialize in different fields. Some will become technicians, some will be medics, experts in toxins, or specialize in working at height, etc. Each can also develop their general skills, such as speed, the effectiveness of escorting civilians to safety, and so on. There are quite many classes and skills to choose from, and in the end [b]two different players can end up with two significantly different crews[/b]. A lot depends on your preferred way of playing. However, there will be challenges more suited for certain classes or approaches. 

At the end of the day, it’s all about discovering it yourself. I will talk more about classes in a separate devlog. Today, I’d rather focus on [b]what this skill system means for the game[/b], and how you, the player, are expected to care for your crew.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165763/fa16d8b1b8496f59059d3608e329f1c22a17d365.jpg[/img]

Some of the many characters you can control in the game. Each of them has their own name and personality. They aren’t just units. They are people, and you need to take care of them.

Every mission, every danger you face, leaves a mark. Your firefighters will become more experienced, but since they’re people, they can also get tired or stressed out. This affects their effectiveness, so you need to choose wisely who you send into action. You can counteract the negative effects with certain additions to your fire station, but this is walking a thin line between having your crew equipped and having them willing to put their lives on the line.

As you see, the three layers of gameplay intertwine, and this will hopefully result in a genuine, thrilling, captivating experience. In real life, firefighting is not just action. It’s a thinking process. I hope that this will shine through Fire Commander’s gameplay, and that it’ll be a worthy tribute to the real world heroes.

If you’re interested in the game and would like to learn more about how we made it, stick around. Follow this page, add Fire Commander to your wishlist. Wishlisting helps us get more visibility on Steam. It’s the easiest way to support a developer you like. Thanks, and see you next time!

notes.title: Welcome to our Fire House!
notes.notes:
Hi, and thanks for checking out our game!  We’re Atomic Wolf, the creators of Fire Commander. We’re sure you have a lot of questions about it. You can check out the Steam description for starters.

If you decide to follow us (by clicking the Follow button on the Steam page), you can expect updates and new gameplay videos or screenshots. But that’s not everything we’d like to talk about. 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1362560/Fire_Commander/][img]https://media.giphy.com/media/8p47l32y8HgU7EobY1/giphy.gif[/img][/url]

You will read about what it means to be a firefighter, what kind of challenges these everyday heroes have to face, and what methods they use in their work. We’d love to make this page the place where we celebrate the courage of real firefighters, and help you discover their occupation.

If you’d like to support us, please add the game to your wishlist. It doesn’t cost you anything, and helps us get more views on Steam. 

Thank you, and see you next time!
